text: Stop 5, downtown's basketball arena.
The real one is the Kaseya Center, home of the Miami Heat.
In the game, it's the Sahara Arena, home of the Vice City Narcos.
Then, in 2026, a helicopter lowered giant pink letters onto the real arena's roof.
They read, welcome to Vice City.
The county's price for that sign?
Just 25,000 below the amount that would have needed a public vote.
But the game's most famous sign was copied from somewhere even stranger.
Stop 6 Miami International Airport.
In the trailer, giant white letters spelling Vice stand at the end of the runway.
The real airport has no sign like that.
But for the movie Bad Boys, Hollywood built one there anyway.
a giant letter spelling Miami, a movie prop that became a video game landmark.

Stop 7.
The Everglades In the game, they're called the Grass Rivers.
That name comes from a 1947 book that called the Everglades a river of grass.
The book helped save the swamp.
The same year, the Everglades became a national park.
The game's swamp has alligators, flamingos, and airboats, just like the real one.
It even hides Burmese pythons in the grass.
In the real Everglades, pythons are an invasive species, pet snakes that escaped and took over.
Head north from the swamp and you hit something much sweeter.
